children: Lula's victory in Brazil's elections at the weekend should trigger disorderly moves in local markets, says Andrea Kiguel, Americas head of rates strategy at Barclays. She expects short-dated bonds could sell off in the order of 300 basis points in the next days, as investors stop out of net received positions. This would be similar to the rates moves in 2022 when Lula announced his cabinet and less constrained spending plans, she adds. Noise around a contested election is typically something markets look through, but could be in the headlines if a potential annulment is discussed, she says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
